title: Delayed Gratification – Proud to Be 'Last to Breaking News'
summary: The Slow Journalism Company publishes 'The European' magazine, taking pride in being deliberately late to breaking news in favor of well-researched, in-depth journalism. Founded in 2012, it counters the 24-hour news cycle with longer publication cycles (monthly or quarterly) to deliver context-rich stories about slow-moving topics like climate change, demographics, and geopolitics.
problem_solved: Solves the problem of superficial, reactive news consumption by providing thoroughly researched, contextual journalism that helps readers understand complex issues over time.
why_valuable: In an era of information overload and breaking news fatigue, it offers a trusted, unhurried alternative that prioritizes accuracy and depth over speed, appealing to readers weary of reactive journalism.
